name: noninterference_idle_tick_moves_no_manager
description: NON-INTERFERENCE, the baseline case: once every state machine has settled, ADVANCING THE CLOCK must not move a single manager. A window sits with keyboard focus on a node; 500 ms of virtual time pass; every one of the fingerprinted managers must read back byte-identical. This is the assertion that establishes the floor — if time alone moves a manager, no other non-interference statement in the suite means anything, because every scenario spends time. Deliberately mouse-free: the headless host re-publishes a hit test whenever a queued window state carries a cursor position, so a scenario that has moved the mouse legitimately moves the hover manager on every tick, and that would be a property of the mouse, not of the clock. Deliberately scroll-container-free: a scrollbar arms a 500 ms fade in gpu_state, and its expiry is real work the clock is supposed to do. min_populated pins the other half — focus IS holding state here, so this is not two empty snapshots comparing equal.
